title: Lab 12 — Quiz 1
subtitle: Unknown ID Part 3 — API 20E and rapid tests

questions.prompt: This strip runs 20 biochemical tests at once on a single pure culture. What is it used to identify?

options.text: Fungi such as Candida and Aspergillus

questions.explanation: API 20E: 20 biochemical tests on a single pure-culture inoculum, used for Enterobacteriaceae (e.g., E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella, Proteus, Klebsiella).

why.D: API 20E tests a pure bacterial culture.

questions.prompt: How is the API 20E result turned into an identification?

options.text: Test results make a 7-digit profile code that is compared with a database
The strip's color matches a single organism directly
The number of positive tests is the species number
The strip is Gram stained after incubation

questions.explanation: Positive results in each section are added to make one digit; the 7-digit profile code is looked up in the API 20E code table/database.

why.B: Results are coded into 7 digits first.
why.C: Positive tests are added within each section.

questions.prompt: How long does API 20E testing take from the patient specimen?

options.text: About 24 hr to isolate a pure culture, then 24 hr incubating the strip
About 15 minutes, like a rapid antigen test
About 5 minutes after dipping the strip
About 1 week, because it needs 20 separate cultures

questions.explanation: The specimen must be streaked for isolation (~24 hr), then the inoculated strip is incubated 24 hr before reading.

why.B: API 20E needs a pure culture and incubation.
why.C: The 5-minute wait is the Quick Strep dipstick.
why.D: All 20 tests run at once on one inoculum.

questions.prompt: API 20E section 1 contains ONPG (1), ADH (2), LDC (4). ONPG and LDC are positive; ADH is negative. What digit goes under section 1?
questions.explanation: Add the numbers of the positive tests in the section: ONPG (1) + LDC (4) = 5.

questions.prompt: API 20E section 2 contains ODC (1), CIT (2), H2S (4). All three are negative. What digit goes under section 2?
questions.explanation: If no test in a section is positive, the digit is 0.

questions.prompt: API 20E section 3 contains URE (1), TDA (2), IND (4). Only IND is positive. What digit goes under section 3?
API 20E section 4 contains VP (1), GEL (2), GLU (4). VP and GLU are positive. What digit goes under section 4?
Read this rapid antigen test: lines at both C and T. What is the result?

options.text: Positive only if the T line is darker

questions.explanation: Test line = antigen detected; control line = the test ran correctly. Both = positive.

why.B: Negative shows only the C line.
why.C: Invalid results have no control (C) line.
why.D: Any visible T line with a C line is positive.

questions.prompt: Read this rapid antigen test: a line at C only. What is the result?
questions.explanation: A control line with no test line = negative.

why.C: A control line is present, so the test is valid.
why.D: C only is a valid negative.

questions.prompt: Read this rapid antigen test: no lines at all. What is the result?

why.A: Negative still shows a control line.
why.D: Without a control line, the test didn't run correctly.

questions.prompt: Read this rapid antigen test: a line at T but NOT at C. What is the result?
questions.explanation: Any result missing the control line is invalid.

why.A: A test line without a control line is invalid.
why.B: Negative shows a C line only.
why.C: Without the control line the result can't be trusted.

questions.prompt: What forms the visible TEST line in a rapid COVID antigen test?

options.text: Control antibodies bound by anti-control antibodies
Patient antibodies bound to the HIV antigen
An immobilized antibody – antigen – labeled antibody 'sandwich'
The absorbent pad soaking up the leftover sample

questions.explanation: SARS-CoV-2 antigen is bound by labeled antibodies, then caught by immobilized antibodies at the test line, forming a colored 'sandwich'.

why.D: The pad just soaks up residual sample.

questions.prompt: Rapid HIV tests like this one detect antibodies. What is the 'false negative window'?

options.text: Time between a positive test and the start of symptoms
Time the strip must sit before reading results
Time between exposure and enough antibodies to reach the detection limit
Time after which the test kit expires

questions.explanation: Antibody-detection tests can be negative early on. HIV tests that detect antigens have a shorter false negative window.

why.A: It's about antibody levels after exposure.
why.B: That's the read time, not the false negative window.
why.D: The window refers to the host's antibody production.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an ANTIGEN detection test?
questions.explanation: Antigen detection examples: pregnancy (HCG), drug tests, food allergens, C. diff toxins, flu, rapid COVID, Quick Strep.

why.C: FeLV is listed under antibody detection.

questions.prompt: Which statement about antibody-based rapid tests is FALSE?

options.text: Culture may be used to confirm a Strep result
They never give false positive or false negative results

questions.explanation: Limitation: false positives and false negatives sometimes happen, so culture may be used for Strep confirmation.
